Could the World Map Change? What the UN's New Move Means for India

2026-09-07 Team Brut UN, Correct the Map, Equal Earth, Mercator, India, world map, cartographic representation, equal-area projection, Jammu and Kashmir, territorial disputes
Read the source article

Quick summary

The UN General Assembly's "Correct the Map" resolution passed 164-1 with six abstentions, encouraging equal-area projections that show Africa's true size, but India's support comes with a caveat about Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh representation.

Key takeaways

  • The UN General Assembly adopted the "Correct the Map" resolution on September 4, 2026, with 164 votes in favor, 1 against (United States), and 6 abstentions
  • The resolution was introduced by Togo on behalf of African countries and encourages wider use of equal-area map projections
  • The Equal Earth projection (2018) preserves relative landmass sizes: Africa appears larger, Europe and North America smaller, India slightly larger
  • The resolution does not ban the Mercator projection or legally require countries to use Equal Earth
  • India voted in favor but clarified it supports equal-area mapping broadly, not one specific projection
  • India demanded any UN-backed map accurately depict Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh per India's official map
